title: Gemini 4 Carbon Tops AI Benchmark by One Point, but Opus Keeps Coding Lead
excerpt: Google's new model leads the Artificial Analysis index and hallucinates far less than Opus 5.5 — though more than its own predecessor. Anthropic still wins on coding agents.
body:
• Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, announced on October 28, leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59 — one point ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 58.
  • On the AA-Omniscience factual test, Carbon scores 54 with an 11% hallucination rate, against 50% for Opus 5.5 — but Carbon's own predecessor, Gemini 4 Argon, hallucinates less, at 4%.
  • Anthropic still leads the work developers pay for most: Opus 5.5 scores 62 to Carbon's 59 on the Coding Agent Index.
  • Carbon became generally available on November 10 on the paid Gemini API, priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, according to pricing coverage.

Google has taken the top spot on the most-watched AI benchmark — by a single point, with an asterisk. Gemini 4 Carbon, announced on October 28 as the second model in the Gemini 4 generation, scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 57, according to Artificial Analysis data reported by TBreak. A revised version of the index, v5.0.1, puts Carbon at 60 and Opus at 59.

The hallucination claim, checked

Much of the launch coverage presents Carbon as the frontier model least likely to make things up. The underlying data supports a narrower claim. On AA-Omniscience, the index component that rewards correct answers and penalises invented ones, Carbon scores 54 — the highest of any model, ahead of Opus 5.5's 48 — and its hallucination rate on that test is 11%, against 50% for both Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. Google says Carbon makes roughly half as many unsupported claims as its predecessor in internal tests. But the predecessor, Gemini 4 Argon, has a hallucination rate of just 4% on the same test: Carbon answers more questions correctly — accuracy rose from 48% to 58% — because it guesses more when it does not know. It is more accurate and less cautious at the same time.

Where Anthropic still wins

On the evaluations closest to paid work, the order reverses. Opus 5.5 leads the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index 62 to 59, and leads on FrontierCode by 56% to 51%, according to comparison coverage of the index data. Carbon posted the best score on four of the index's nine evaluations, including science and automation tasks.

Who can actually use it

Carbon's rollout was staged: Google first offered it to a subset of cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program, with wider trusted-partner access to follow. Pricing and availability coverage records general availability from November 10, 2026, as gemini-4-carbon on the Gemini API's paid tier and in Google AI Studio, at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30 — half Opus 5.5's list price — with the two models priced identically from December 1.

The bottom line for buyers

For factual question-answering and research workloads, Carbon's combination of a higher accuracy rate and a far lower hallucination rate than Opus is the strongest practical claim in the launch. For coding agents, Anthropic's lead holds. And the one-point index gap is inside the range where benchmark revisions reorder the table — as the move from v5.0 to v5.0.1 already showed.
